azure-cloud: The Azure & Cloud track covers Microsoft's exams for people who run, build and design solutions on Azure. It starts with the fundamentals exam, AZ-900, and moves through administration (AZ-104), solution design (AZ-305) and DevOps (AZ-400). Specialist exams sit alongside them: AZ-700 for networking, AZ-120 for SAP workloads on Azure, AZ-140 for Azure Virtual Desktop and AZ-802 for Windows Server administration.

This track suits cloud and systems administrators, solution architects, DevOps engineers, network engineers and IT staff who are moving workloads to the cloud. If you are new to Azure, AZ-900 teaches the vocabulary of cloud computing and the core Azure services without asking for hands-on experience, so it is a sensible first step.

A common order is to take AZ-900 if you are new to cloud, then AZ-104 if you administer Azure resources day to day. After that, choose the exam that matches your role: AZ-305 to design solutions, AZ-400 for DevOps practices, or AZ-700 for networking. Open any exam below for its official skills and weightings, a week-by-week study plan and free practice questions with explanations, so you can see where you stand before you book.

The same themes return across these exams: identity and governance, storage, compute, networking, monitoring and cost control. If you learn them well for AZ-900 and AZ-104, the later exams build on them instead of starting again, so the time you spend on the foundations pays off several times over.
security-identity: The Security & Identity track covers Microsoft's exams on protecting systems, managing who can access them and keeping data compliant. SC-900 is the fundamentals exam. The role-based exams include SC-200 for security operations analysts, SC-300 for identity and access administrators, SC-401 for information security administrators working with Microsoft 365, SC-100 for cybersecurity architects and SC-500 for security controls across cloud and AI workloads.

These exams suit security analysts, identity administrators, compliance officers, architects who design security into systems, and IT staff who are taking on security duties. SC-900 asks for no hands-on experience, which makes it a good first step if you are moving into security from another area of IT.

A practical order is SC-900 for the concepts, then the role exam that matches your job: SC-200 if you investigate and respond to threats, SC-300 if you manage identities and access, or SC-401 if you protect and govern information. SC-100 is aimed at people who design security architecture and is usually taken after you have worked in one of those roles. Each exam page lists Microsoft's skills with their weightings and offers free practice questions with explanations.

The same ideas run through every security exam: least privilege, defence in depth, detection and response, and data protection. Learn them once for SC-900 and each later exam applies them to a narrower role, so your study time carries over from one exam to the next.
microsoft-365: The Microsoft 365 track covers the administration side of Microsoft's productivity platform. It includes MS-102 for Microsoft 365 administrators, MD-102 for managing and securing endpoints with Intune, MS-700 for managing Microsoft Teams and MS-721 for collaboration communications systems engineers. Together they cover tenants, devices, collaboration and voice.

These exams suit Microsoft 365 administrators, desktop and endpoint engineers, Teams administrators and communications engineers. They are most useful if you already spend time in the Microsoft 365 admin centres, because the questions are written around real administration tasks rather than definitions.

Start with the exam closest to your daily work. Tenant-wide administrators usually begin with MS-102, endpoint and device teams with MD-102, and collaboration teams with MS-700 or MS-721. Microsoft revises these exams often, and some are being retired and replaced, so check the notice on each exam page and the date of its skills outline before you book. Every page here shows the official skills and weightings, a study plan and free practice questions with explanations.

Hands-on practice matters more here than in most tracks. A trial or developer tenant lets you use the admin centres yourself, and exam questions often describe a situation and ask which setting or policy fixes it. Reading about a setting helps, but having changed it yourself is what makes the answer obvious under time pressure.
power-platform: The Power Platform track covers Microsoft's low-code tools: Power Apps, Power Automate, Power BI and Copilot Studio. PL-900 is the fundamentals exam that introduces all of them. PL-300 is the Power BI data analyst exam, and PL-400 covers development with the Power Platform; check its exam page, because Microsoft has retired it.

These exams suit business analysts, citizen developers, data analysts and consultants who build apps, automate processes or report on data without writing a full application from scratch. PL-900 needs no hands-on experience and works well as a first step for people in business roles.

A common order is PL-900 for the overview, then PL-300 if your work is data and reporting. If you build apps and automations, look at the current exams listed on Microsoft Learn for that role and use the guides here to see what each one measures. Each exam page below shows Microsoft's skills with their weightings, a study plan and free practice questions with explanations so you can test yourself before you book.

Hands-on practice helps in this track as well. The Power Platform is easy to try for free, and building a small app, a flow and a report teaches you how the exams ask their questions better than reading alone. Use the practice questions afterwards to find the topics your small projects did not cover.
dynamics-365: The Dynamics 365 track covers Microsoft's business applications for finance, supply chain, customer service and small-business accounting. The exams include MB-230 for customer service functional consultants, MB-310 for finance, MB-330 for supply chain management, MB-500 for finance and operations apps developers, MB-800 for Business Central functional consultants and MB-820 for Business Central developers.

These exams suit functional consultants who configure Dynamics 365 for a business, developers who extend it, and finance or operations staff who administer it. They assume you have worked with the application, because the questions describe business scenarios and ask which configuration or customisation solves them.

Choose by role and by product. Functional consultants take the MB-230, MB-310, MB-330 or MB-800 exam for the application they implement, and developers take MB-500 or MB-820 for Finance and Operations or Business Central. Many people take a consultant exam first and a developer exam later. Open an exam below for its official skills and weightings, a study plan and free practice questions with explanations.

Because the questions are scenario based, the best preparation mixes reading with time in a demo or trial environment of the application. Work through one business process from start to finish, such as order to cash, and then use practice questions to check the terminology and the options the exam expects you to know.
data-ai: The Data & AI track covers Microsoft's exams on databases, analytics, data engineering and artificial intelligence on Azure. DP-900 and AI-901 are the fundamentals exams for data and AI. The role-based exams include DP-300 for Azure SQL administration, DP-420 for Azure Cosmos DB, DP-600 and DP-700 for analytics and data engineering with Microsoft Fabric, DP-750 for Azure Databricks, DP-800 for AI-enabled database solutions and the AI-103, AI-200, AI-300 and AI-500 exams for building and operating AI solutions.

These exams suit database administrators, data engineers, analytics engineers, developers adding AI to applications, and machine learning engineers who run models in production. The fundamentals exams ask for no hands-on experience and are a good starting point if you are moving into data or AI from another IT role.

A practical order is DP-900 or AI-901 for the concepts, then the exam that matches what you build: DP-300 if you administer databases, DP-600 or DP-700 if you work in Microsoft Fabric, or one of the AI exams if you develop AI applications. Microsoft is adding and revising exams in this area quickly, so each page shows the date of the official skills outline. Every exam page has the skills and weightings, a study plan and free practice questions with explanations.

Whichever exam you choose, plan for hands-on time. Data and AI services change quickly and the exams ask about current behaviour, so work with the services in a free or trial subscription and check the date on the official skills outline. Then use the practice questions to find the gaps between what you built and what the outline asks.
more-exams: This section holds Microsoft exams that do not belong to one of the main tracks. It includes the GitHub exams (GH-100, GH-200, GH-300, GH-500, GH-600 and GH-900), the AI business exams (AB-100, AB-210, AB-250, AB-410, AB-620, AB-650, AB-730, AB-731 and AB-900) and a few older or specialist exams.

The GitHub exams suit developers, DevOps engineers and administrators who work with GitHub Actions, GitHub Copilot, advanced security and enterprise administration. The AB exams suit business and technology leaders, solution architects and administrators who plan, build or manage AI and Copilot solutions inside Microsoft 365 and Dynamics 365.

Pick the exam that matches the tools you use. If you are new to GitHub, GH-900 is the foundations exam. For AI in business, AB-730 and AB-731 are aimed at professionals and leaders, while the other AB exams are role-based. Some exams here have been retired or replaced, so read the notice on the exam page and the date of its skills outline. Each page shows the official skills with weightings, a study plan and free practice questions with explanations.

Whichever exam you choose, start from the official skills outline that the exam page links to, and use the study plan on each page to spread the topics across the weeks. Then test yourself with the free practice questions and read every explanation, including the ones for questions you answered correctly.
